# Steven Kleynenberg — UnLinked

> Architecting sovereign AI systems, patented NLP retrieval engines (WO2014003543A1), and massively parallel software — without platform lock-in or algorithmic noise.

- **Canonical Portal**: https://kleynenberg.github.io/
- **Location**: Delft, South Holland, The Netherlands
- **Role**: Principal enterprise and AI architect, parallel computing researcher and independent publisher
- **Active Flagship**: Project UnLinked — who needs walled-garden platforms when we have AI? (https://kleynenberg.github.io/)

## Core Ecosystem Links

- [taksie.ai](https://taksie.ai): AI fiscal pre-processor
- [innopheon](https://innopheon.com): Enterprise intelligence and patent analytics

- [naaap.io](https://naaap.io): Autonomous audiovisual network
- [GitHub](https://github.com/kleynenberg): Public source repositories

## Flagship Initiative: Project UnLinked

An experimental demonstration of post-platform professional identity: raw primary sources—academic proceedings, WIPO patent records, ISO C syntax artifacts, and active software inventories—distilled with AI assistance into a deterministic, zero-dependency HTML5/CSS3/JS Progressive Web App with full Schema.org JSON-LD and llms.txt semantic indexing.

## Pillar #1 — Chronological Academic, Defence & Enterprise Foundation (1985–2020)

### 1985 – 1993 — Co-founder and software developer — Kleynenberg & Kleynenberg
- **Organization**: Kleynenberg & Kleynenberg (Naarden, The Netherlands)
- **Summary**: Co-founded and operated a commercial custom software consultancy alongside his father at the outset of his university studies.
  - Engineered mission-critical bespoke business applications and relational database systems for SME clients.
  - Built low-level performance-critical routines in ANSI C, dBase, and 80x86 assembly environments.

### 1986 – 1991 — Academic specialization — computer science, AI and complex systems
- **Organization**: Leiden University and Delft University of Technology
- **Summary**: Specialized in computer science, artificial intelligence, theoretical psychology, and complex dynamical systems.
  - Focused on connectionist neural architectures, modular cognitive modeling, and parallel execution topologies.
  - Reference: [Leiden University](https://www.universiteitleiden.nl)
  - Reference: [Delft University of Technology](https://www.tudelft.nl)

### 1988 – 1991 — Architect — CALM development system and MetaNet network environment
- **Organization**: Leiden University (in collaboration with Jacob M. J. Murre)
- **Summary**: Designed and implemented a machine-independent, modular software environment for specifying, compiling, and simulating neural networks.
  - Authored the MetaNet specification language, graphical topology editor, network compiler, and hardware abstraction layer.
  - Implemented a 4-layer execution architecture (POINTs, dataflow, DEL, and DCA) supporting T800 Transputers and vector hardware.
  - Published and presented findings at INNC-90-Paris (1990) and ICANN-91 in Espoo / Helsinki, Finland (1991).
  - Reference: [IEEE Xplore](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org)
  - Reference: [Aalto University (ICANN-91 Host)](https://www.aalto.fi)

### 1991 — Hardware-software integration — BSP400 400-processor neurocomputer
- **Organization**: Leiden University / IEEE IJCNN 1991
- **Summary**: Integrated the MetaNet network environment with the massively parallel 400-processor BSP400 neurocomputer architecture.
  - Bridged high-level modular neural network definitions directly onto dedicated parallel neurocomputer hardware.
  - Published in the IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN 1991) proceedings.
  - Reference: [ResearchGate profile](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Steven-Kleynenberg)
  - Reference: [IEEE Xplore](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org)

### 1991 – 1993 — Visiting researcher — massively parallel Connection Machine supercomputing
- **Organization**: Mathematical Institute, Rheinische Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität Bonn (Germany)
- **Summary**: Developed an object-oriented neural network simulation framework executing on the Connection Machine supercomputer.
  - Engineered fine-grained data-parallel abstractions for large-scale connectionist simulations at the Mathematical Institute Bonn.
  - Reference: [University of Bonn](https://www.uni-bonn.de)

### 1991 – 1994 — Lead systems architect — Abrams Main Battle Tank (MBT) diagnostic expert system
- **Organization**: Netherlands Ministry of Defence and Leiden University
- **Summary**: Designed and delivered a Model-Based Reasoning (MBR) diagnostic expert system for the Abrams Main Battle Tank.
  - Built deterministic fault-isolation models meeting stringent military security, reliability, and zero-defect operational standards.
  - Reference: [Netherlands Ministry of Defence](https://www.defensie.nl)

### 1991 – 1994 — Real-time software architect — TCAS air traffic collision avoidance system
- **Organization**: Civil Aviation Authority and Leiden University
- **Summary**: Developed real-time conflict-detection algorithms and radar operator interface architectures for national air traffic control.
  - Engineered low-latency trajectory evaluation routines and high-clarity radar situational displays.

### 1992 – 1995 — Chief architect — distributed cellular automata traffic infrastructure simulation
- **Organization**: TU Delft, Leiden University and Ministry of Transport, Public Works and Water Management
- **Summary**: Architected a distributed, agent-based cellular automata simulation platform for next-generation national traffic management.
  - Modeled emergent macroscopic traffic flow dynamics from local microscopic vehicle rules across distributed compute nodes.
  - Reference: [Delft University of Technology](https://www.tudelft.nl)

### 1993 – 1996 — Systems software developer — C/C++ enterprise architecture
- **Organization**: Rijnhaave Automatisering (Zoetermeer, The Netherlands)
- **Summary**: Specialized in C and C++ systems engineering and mission-critical enterprise software architecture.
  - Delivered high-throughput transactional modules and cross-platform C/C++ middleware components.

### October 1996 – December 2020 — Principal architect and AI/NLP lead
- **Organization**: Sopheon N.V.
- **Summary**: Led long-term technological vision, software architecture, and AI/NLP retrieval engines for Enterprise Innovation Management over a 24-year tenure.
  - Architected large-scale linguistic indexing, automated knowledge discovery, and enterprise decision-support platforms.
  - Established core text-mining pipelines powering Sopheon Monitor Express and patent intelligence workflows.
  - Reference: [Sopheon](https://www.sopheon.com)

### 2014 — Co-inventor — international patent WO2014003543A1 (POS-tagging document retrieval)
- **Organization**: WIPO / Sopheon N.V. (with Elsemiek ten Pas and Huub Rutten)
- **Summary**: Co-invented international patent WO2014003543A1 automating large-scale document retrieval and linguistic text mining via Part-of-Speech tagging.
  - Provides the foundational algorithmic architecture for automated technical concept extraction and patent landscape analysis.
  - Reference: [Google Patents WO2014003543A1](https://patents.google.com/patent/WO2014003543A1/en)

### 2000 – 2020 — Technical lead and cross-border architect — European Commission and ITEA consortia
- **Organization**: EU FP5 / ITEA2 / ITEA3 Consortia (Sopheon N.V., AMC, Philips Healthcare, Technolution)
- **Summary**: Directed distributed systems architecture across five multi-year European research and medical HPC programs.
  - LORE (IST-1999-12645, 2000–2002): Leveraging Operational Resource Expertise — EU-funded knowledge retrieval and team coordination.
  - Edafmis (2008–2012): Embedded Decision and Data Fusion for Medical Intervention Support.
  - MEDUSA (2013–2015, ITEA2 10004): Medical Distributed Utilization of Services & Applications — cloud-based acute stroke care decision support (Node.js DSS and WebGL 3D Segmentation Renderer) with AMC, Philips Healthcare, Prologue, Bull, Telecom SudParis, and Technolution (ESOCC 2015, LNCS 9306).
  - Medolution (2015–2019): Connected medical infrastructure, real-time telemetry, and clinical decision support.
  - PARTNER (2017–2020): Large-scale collaborative data integration and decision-support platform.
  - Reference: [EU CORDIS](https://cordis.europa.eu)
  - Reference: [ITEA4 Sopheon N.V. Dossier](https://itea4.org/organisation/2051-sopheon-n-v.html)
  - Reference: [MEDUSA ESOCC 2015 Publication](https://pure.amsterdamumc.nl/en/publications/remote-collaboration-decision-support-and-on-demand-medical-image/)

## Scientific Publications Archive

- **KLP-1990-INNC (1990)**: *The MetaNet network environment for the development of modular neural networks* — Steven E. Kleynenberg, Jacob M. J. Murre. Proceedings of the International Neural Network Conference (INNC-90-Paris), Paris, France.
  - Archive URL: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org
  - Abstract: Presents the MetaNet network environment, a modular specification language, graphical topology editor, and hardware-independent compiler designed for constructing and simulating complex modular neural networks such as CALM architectures.
- **KLP-1991-ICANN (1991)**: *Extending the MetaNet Network Environment: process control and machine independence* — Steven E. Kleynenberg, Jacob M. J. Murre. Proceedings of the International Conference on Artificial Neural Networks (ICANN-91), Espoo / Helsinki, Finland.
  - Archive URL: https://www.aalto.fi
  - Abstract: Introduces explicit process-control primitives and a four-layer hardware abstraction pipeline (POINTs, dataflow, DEL, and DCA) enabling identical MetaNet neural network specifications to execute across sequential workstations, Transputer arrays, and vector processors.
- **KLP-1991-IJCNN (1991)**: *Integrating the BSP400 neurocomputer with the MetaNet network environment* — Steven E. Kleynenberg, Jacob M. J. Murre. Proceedings of the IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN 1991).
  - Archive URL: https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Steven-Kleynenberg
  - Abstract: Details the compiler backend and runtime bridge connecting the high-level MetaNet specification environment with the massively parallel 400-processor BSP400 neurocomputer.
- **KLP-2015-ESOCC (2015)**: *Remote Collaboration, Decision Support, and On-Demand Medical Image Analysis for Acute Stroke Care* — Renan Sales Barros, Jordi Borst, Steven Kleynenberg, Céline Badr, Rama-Rao Ganji, Hubrecht de Bliek, Landry-Stéphane Zeng-Eyindanga, Henk van den Brink, Charles Majoie, Henk Marquering, Sílvia Delgado Olabarriaga. European Conference on Service-Oriented and Cloud Computing (ESOCC 2015), Springer LNCS 9306, pp. 214–225.
  - DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-24072-5_15
  - Archive URL: https://pure.amsterdamumc.nl/en/publications/remote-collaboration-decision-support-and-on-demand-medical-image/
  - Abstract: Presents the cloud-based Medical Distributed Utilization of Services & Applications (MEDUSA) platform and Acute Stroke Prototype (MSP), combining GPU-accelerated medical image processing, Sopheon's Node.js rule-based Decision Support System (DSS), and a browser-native WebGL 3D Segmentation Renderer.

## Pillar #2 — Living R&D Sandbox (2020–Present)

- **taksie.ai** (https://taksie.ai) [Active]: AI-driven fiscal pre-processor and structured tax optimization engine engineered for Dutch income tax workflows.
- **innopheon & Innopheon2 (Phoenix / Fenix & Monitor Express)** (https://innopheon.com) [Active]: Next-generation patent intelligence, POS-tagging natural language query workspace (Solr/SumoBrain), and innovation monitoring platform.
- **4D Scatter (4D-scatter)** [R&D]: Interactive multidimensional visual analytics engine for exploring high-dimensional scientific and telemetry datasets.
- **Parallel fractal and mathematical compute engines** [R&D]: Real-time GPU-accelerated mathematical rendering and parallel compute kernels built on WebGL and WebGPU.
- **gpuspeech** [Open-source R&D]: Open-source Chrome extension leveraging WebGPU and offscreen documents for hardware-accelerated browser-native text-to-speech synthesis.
- **Offline AR star-mapping PWA** [R&D]: Zero-dependency astronomical Augmented Reality PWA computing Local Sidereal Time, Julian dates, and quaternion sensor fusion offline.
- **Synaptix Studio (formerly MetaNet PWA)** [R&D]: Spartan browser-native visual neural network topology editor and forward-propagation simulator inspired by MetaNet.
- **MetroMoo** (https://moo.demetro.nl) [Live]: Cloud-native re-engineering of classic LambdaMOO into a serverless WebSocket/JSON architecture with BigQuery event sourcing and WebGL cartography.
- **AudioTap and Linux guitar DSP pipeline** [Active]: Real-time low-latency audio capture, PipeWire signal routing, REAPER integration, and Roland G-303 synthesizer guitar emulation on Fedora Linux.
- **AutoIngest** [Active]: Automated multimedia and textual ingestion, transcription, and semantic enrichment pipeline.
- **Zephyr2026 biometric telemetry** [R&D]: Real-time physiological sensor ingestion and telemetry analysis for Zephyr BioHarness and Polar H7 heart-rate hardware.
- **Hardware flashing orchestration (make.py & Arduino TUI-flasher)** [Active]: Terminal-first build and firmware flashing orchestration for microcontrollers, LoRa Marvin boards, and Coolsand hardware.
- **SteveOS (32-bit x86 operating system kernel)** [Active]: Custom bare-metal 32-bit x86 kernel authored from scratch in NASM assembly and C featuring a deterministic flat filesystem.
- **Security forensics and sovereign infrastructure automation** [Active]: Deep system forensics, automated Apache/SSL virtual-host provisioning (make_vhosts_domain on Fedora), and crypto network telemetry (cryptosum.pay).
